summary: A Discord server can name one channel for all music announcements, instead of them landing wherever the first play happened to run.
details: Set `music_channel = "<channel id>"` on a room in `policy.toml` and every music announcement for that server — the now-playing line when a track ends and the next one starts, the autoplay line, what follows a skip, and the notice when the voice connection drops — is posted in that channel.
The named channel is a destination, not a room: Nora posts to it and never reads it. It may not be a channel listed in `policy.toml`, and a server that names one is refused at startup.
A server that sets nothing is unchanged: announcements keep going to the channel the session started in.
At most one room per server may name a channel; a second is refused at startup rather than resolved by picking one.
If the named channel cannot be posted to — deleted, no permission, or in a different server — the announcement goes to the channel the session started in instead, and says so in the log.
limitations: System announcements only. A slash command still replies in the channel you typed it in, and Nora's own reply when you ask her to play something still lands in the room you asked from.
Naming the channel does not restrict who may start music: `/music play` still works from any channel in a server Nora is allowed to join voice in.
Changing the channel needs a restart, the same as every other `policy.toml` change.
